listing.name: Wipeout XL / Alexbeav PSXRecomp
listing.summary: PlayStation port prepared with your own matching disc and any required BIOS. Complete setup with the project’s launcher; you manage this copy, its updates and your saved data.

steps.title: Unpack the stable setup kit
steps.instruction: Extract the complete ZIP for your system into a writable folder. Choose the Intel or Apple silicon ZIP that matches your Mac. Check the release notes for that kit’s prerequisites.

steps.title: Install the build tools
steps.instruction: On Windows, install Python 3. The upstream wizard downloads the build-tool pack on first rebuild. On Linux and Mac, put CMake, Ninja, a supported Python 3 version and a native C/C++ compiler on PATH.

steps.title: Supply the matching original files
steps.instruction: Select your own Wipeout XL (USA).cue (SCUS-94351) with all 12 referenced BIN tracks. The v0.1.2 kit requires your own 524,288-byte SCPH-1001 (USA) retail BIOS with SHA-256 71af94d1e47a68c11e8fdb9f8368040601514a42a5a399cda48c7d3bff1e99d3.

steps.title: Build and add the completed player
steps.instruction: Run Wipeout_XL_Recompiled from the kit folder, with .exe on Windows. Choose Generate & rebuild. Select the completed player under build-release in Portcove and use build-release as its start folder.

warnings: Check the README-SETUP.txt inside your exact kit for its BIOS requirement. Older kits can require a different dump. Keep the original files and the working kit together.
Portcove has not verified native setup, gameplay or save compatibility.

references.title: Check Linux and Mac prerequisites
references.instruction: Check the release notes for the kit’s Python version, macOS minimum and required libraries before starting setup. The v0.1.2 kits need Python 3.10 or newer on Linux and Mac. The Mac setup uses Apple clang 15 and needs Homebrew’s OpenSSL, FreeType and HarfBuzz libraries.

references.title: Keep your working copy and data
references.instruction: Make an in-game save and close the player before updating. Back up the whole working folder, including memory cards, settings, keyboard profiles, replays and mods you use. Keep your original disc and BIOS. Save states and replays can depend on the build.
